title: Multi‐stage chemically modified waste sunflower oil as an industrial base‐stock for metal‐working fluid
content:
Abstract

Environmental concerns and the depletion of fossil fuels are driving an emerging trend toward using vegetable oils as a viable base stock for industrial metalworking fluids (MWF). Several edible and non-edible oil sources have been identified as renewable base stocks for the manufacture of bio-lubricants and green metalworking fluids. Sunflower oil (SO) is a good lubricant; however, the cost of pure sunflower oil is very high. Considering the economic concerns, it is not practical to use pure sunflower oil as a base oil for metal-working fluid application. Whereas, waste cooking sunflower oil (WSO) can be a viable replacement. The main drawback of WSO is its low oxidation stability and poor tribological properties. This study evaluated and compared the lubricating qualities of waste sunflower oil (WSO), transesterified waste sunflower oil (TWSO), and esterification followed by transesterification of waste sunflower oil (ETWSO). The experimental results showed that the ETWSO exhibits a reduced wear scar diameter and a lower coefficient of friction, indicating better tribological performance than WSO. The Hot Oil Oxidation Test (HOOT) result showed that ETWSO has better oxidative stability compared to WSO. The formulated green metal-working fluid exhibited better tribological performance and corrosive stability compared to commercially available metal-working oil.
